Plan next season's buy
what the stylists use that we do not sell, what nobody styled, what each occasion leans on
Feature the brand's signature pieces and pairings
which pieces hold the most looks together, which pairings are the signature

what should sit next to this piece on the page

is this new photo on-brand

what is emerging, what is our style per occasion, where the lookbook is thin
Run analytics on the graph data
Tab 3. Counts and comparisons in openCypher, every answer with its rows.
Find what looks or reads alike
Tab 4. Embedding similarity over the garments and looks.

Tabs 4 and 5. The graph walk behind GraphRAG; every suggestion names its look.
Group what is alike and explain the groups with the graph
Tab 6. Clusters of embeddings, read with the graph data.
Where the graph comes from
All of it reads the graph that tabs 1 and 2 built by breaking every photo down with the ontology.
